summary: H.R. 7386 extends the authorization of the First Responder Network Authority (FirstNet Authority) through September 30, 2037, and changes how it is managed. It removes the FirstNet Authority's independent status, making its actions subject to approval by the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA). The bill also adds requirements for outage notifications, business continuity and disaster recovery plans, board member composition, annual reports to Congress, and contractor evaluations.

affected_groups.effect: Its independent agency status is removed, its operations are placed under NTIA approval, and its authorization is extended to 2037.
Must submit multi-year disaster recovery plans, provide 30-minute outage notifications, supply a network status tool to users, and face performance evaluations.
Represented by a larger number of professionals on the FirstNet Board and provided with a status tool for monitoring network outages.
Assumes management and approval responsibilities over the FirstNet Authority and must submit annual reports and briefings to Congress.

key_provisions: Extends the FirstNet Authority through September 30, 2037, and removes its independent agency status, placing its operations under the NTIA.
Establishes an Associate Administrator position within the NTIA to manage FirstNet operations.
Requires the Board of the FirstNet Authority to include at least five public safety professionals from state, local, or tribal backgrounds.
Requires the network contractor to notify the FirstNet Authority of any confirmed unscheduled outage within 30 minutes and provide users with a network status tool.
Requires the contractor to submit a business continuity and disaster recovery plan to the NTIA every five years.
Mandates annual reports to Congress from the NTIA regarding cybersecurity, network adoption rates, and unscheduled outages.
Requires the Government Accountability Office to report within seven years on recommendations for Congress regarding the termination of the FirstNet Authority.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 7386 extends the authorization of the First Responder Network Authority (FirstNet Authority) through September 30, 2037, and changes how it is managed. It removes the FirstNet Authority's independent status, making its actions subject to approval by the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA). The bill also adds requirements for outage notifications, business continuity and disaster recovery plans, board member composition, annual reports to Congress, and contractor evaluations.
summary_detail.significance: This bill reauthorizes and alters the governance of the nationwide public safety broadband network for over a decade, increasing federal oversight via the NTIA and establishing stricter reporting, cybersecurity, and disaster recovery requirements for network operators.
